title: Chu Berry's death and the minute of silence in Montreal
summary: Chu died days later; Calloway waited until after the dance in Montreal to announce it and hired a replacement.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: But he was out of his mind. He didn't really know what he was doing.
That's right. That's right. He sure did.
That was a very sad moment for us. We found out on the job up in Canada two or three days later, remember, when he died?
Sure, we played Toronto and then we went on to Kingston and from Kingston we went to Montreal.
And that night Calloway waited till after the dance.
And he told the people, he said, 'Now we'll have a minute's silence for a brother of ours that passed this morning.' And we didn't know that Calloway had sent and got his mother --
-- and got his wife, Jerrie, to be at the hospital there when he died, you know. And that's when he sent and got McGray, Teddy McGray in Chee's place.
